newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Brierley rejects Delham strife rumours.
newsitem.headline: Brierley rejects Delham strife rumours.

text.p: New Zealand-based Brierley Investments Ltd's chairman Bob Matthew rejected as entirely untrue market rumours of strife in relations between Brierley and its 20 percent shareholder, the Delham consortium from Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia.
"I've heard those mutterings and they're entirely untrue," Matthew told Reuters in an interview.
"We have close and cordial relationships with several members of the Delham consortium," he said.
Matthew said both groups aimed to make profits by quietly seeking out investment opportunities that others did not see.
"The relative silence that you've heard is synonomous with them and us getting on in that way," he said.

The Delham consortium is made up of Hong Leong Industries Bhd group of Malaysia, Sembawang Corp of Singapore, Salim Group of Indonesia and Haw Par Brothers International Ltd and Hong Leong of Singapore.
Matthew said Brierley's closer links with some of the five did not mean that Brierley did not get on with the others.
"No. There are two or three out of the five that we have particular projects with," he said.
Delham holds its shareholding in Brierley through Malex Industries Bhd.
